objectives.text: Keep the Taiwan tie, which pays. Eswatini has recognised the Republic of China since 1968 and is the last African state still doing so; Taipei's aid and trade are the return. The April 2026 visit by Taiwan's president, cancelled after overflight was revoked, shows how much the tie depends on others' airspace.

grand_strategy.reading: Eswatini is an absolute monarchy with no treaty partner to protect it, so it trades what it has: a recognition of Taiwan that Beijing would like to buy, and a place for deportees that Washington pays for in secret. Taipei is the patron the state has kept since 1968, and the United States is the new one, paying for a service no one else is offering. The weak point is that both bargains rest on others' airspace, courts and goodwill rather than on anything Eswatini controls.

stances.note: Recognition since 16 September 1968, which makes Taiwan the patron. Partner, no treaty: the tie is aid and trade for recognition. Evidence mirrored from the Taiwanese card (TWN toward SWZ, same sources), read here as Eswatini's side. Trend stable on the Mbabane side: the April 2026 cancellation of Taiwan's visit was an access problem for Taipei (overflight), not a sign that Eswatini moved. Bond none: no kinship, no open grievance.

stances_toward.note: Partner, stable. Eswatini sits in SACU and the rand area, and Ramaphosa attended the commemoration of King Mswati III's coronation (SAnews listing; the date of the page was not confirmed, hence the year only). The sore point is the US third-country deportation deal: Eswatini has taken several groups of deportees since July 2025 (AP), and one outlet alleges some crossed into South Africa (not verified). South African exports to Eswatini were about USD 1.93bn in 2025 (Trading Economics, tier 4). Thin on purpose: the sources seen are a listing and a wire story, and the Wikipedia article on the pair (tier 4) is only an index. Grade partner is our reading. Bond none.
